title: Inflation of a stretched Mooney–Rivlin tube (follower pressure)
source: Finite inflation and extension of an incompressible Mooney–Rivlin tube (R. S. Rivlin, Large elastic deformations of isotropic materials VI, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 242:173–195, 1949; R. W. Ogden, Non-Linear Elastic Deformations, Dover 1997, §5.3): at axial stretch λ_z, r² = a² + (R² − A²)/λ_z, σ_θ − σ_r = 2 (λ_θ² − λ_r²)(C₁₀ + C₀₁ λ_z²) with λ_θ = r/R, λ_r = 1/(λ_θ λ_z), integrated through the wall: p = ∫ (σ_θ − σ_r) dr/r (Simpson, 2·10⁵ intervals)

quantities.quantity: radial displacement of the bore (10, 0, 0) at the pressure that inflates it to a = 15 at λ_z = 1.5
quantities.reason: 16 × 6 hybrid hex20 around the quarter; ν = 0.4995 stands in for incompressibility (a volume change of order p/κ ≈ 10⁻³ shifts the radii by about 0.1 %), and the tube is stretched axially by its ends, which a nearly incompressible solid takes with larger pressures than the plane-strain neo-Hookean tube

quantities.quantity: radial displacement of the outer wall (20, 0, 0): b − B, a small difference of radii
quantities.reason: 0.2 % of the outer radius b = 20.616: the same volume change of order 10⁻³ moves b by about 0.03, which is 4.5 % of b − B; the incompressible kinematics r² = a² + (R² − A²)/λ_z amplify it there
